description: Kaminskiy Design & Remodeling is the San Diego-based home-improvement brand founded by Sergei Kaminskiy in 2005; its franchise arm, Kaminskiy Care and Repair, was formed as Kaminskiy Franchise Group, LLC (Frisco, Texas) in October 2024 and began offering franchises in its 2024 Franchise Disclosure Document (issued November 4, 2024). Franchisees operate a residential and business repair, maintenance and improvement business under the Kaminskiy Care and Repair name - the brand's 'small jobs, big difference' model covers doors, drywall, paint, fences, dry rot and termite repair, and full to-do-list handyman work, with a workmanship warranty and licensed, bonded and insured crews. The FDD discloses zero litigation and zero bankruptcies (Items 3-4), a $74,995 franchise fee, $166,495 to $195,495 estimated initial investment, 7% royalty, and a Designated Territory of roughly 40,000-60,000 target households. At issuance the system had 5 company-owned outlets and zero third-party franchisees; Item 19 reports 2023 average gross revenue of $850,185 across two company-owned outlets (San Diego $1,217,466, East Bay $482,904).
territoryDescription: Upon securing the Approved Location, the franchisor grants a Designated Territory (described by zip codes or geographical boundaries) in which the franchisee has protected rights: while in compliance, the franchisor will not own, operate, franchise or license any other Franchised Businesses inside the territory. The protection is not absolute — the territory may overlap with other franchisees' or affiliate-owned locations, and the franchisor reserves broad rights including merger/acquisition activity under other marks, being acquired by a competing business, and selling through alternative channels (mail order, catalog, telemarketing, internet, e-commerce, retail) inside or outside the territory, with no compensation owed to the franchisee. A typical territory holds 40,000-60,000 target households. Territory rights are not tied to sales volume, and the franchisee has no right to additional territories or alternate distribution channels. Classified as non-exclusive. (FDD Item 12, pp.28-30)
